name: Palace Lantern
description: In the early Ming Dynasty, there was a scholar who was the number one scholar in high school. The emperor wanted to recruit him as his consort, but the number one scholar asked him to marry the girl who had accompanied him when he was studying hard. The emperor was moved by his sincerity of not forgetting his original intention. Not only did he agree to the marriage, but he also ordered someone to make a gilt palace lantern and give it to the couple, which meant that the light was shining brightly, the future was bright, and they would be happy together. This palace lantern is carved with dragons and phoenixes, inlaid with silver and precious stones, and painted with pictures of flowers, birds, auspicious animals, and beauties. It is ingenious and beautiful. Later, it was spread among the people that when a couple got married, hanging palace lanterns high represented the blessing of loving each other and holding hands and growing old.
